status: DRAFT for team review (Shadi, 2026-10-31). Control families are Category E (Defense & Governance) controls, one per Mapper sub-cluster. OWASP IDs use the Mapper's OWASP LLM Top 10 (2026) numbering.

AI-assisted phishing.description: Filter and authenticate inbound messages, and train users to verify unusual requests, since AI-written lures remove the usual spelling and tone cues.
containment_steps: Quarantine the message and every copy delivered to other mailboxes, and block the sender domain and any links or attachments.
Identify users who clicked or replied; reset their credentials and revoke active sessions.
Check mail and sign-in logs for follow-on activity from the same campaign and warn affected teams.

AI-assisted fraud & deepfakes.description: Require out-of-band confirmation and liveness or document checks for high-value requests, because voice, video and documents can be synthesized.
containment_steps: Freeze the requested transaction, account change or onboarding until identity is confirmed through a separate, known channel.
Preserve the audio, video or documents used, and flag the identity data as compromised.
Review other requests from the same identity, device or session for the same pattern.

AI-assisted malware.control_family: Endpoint detection and AI-API egress monitoring
AI-assisted malware.description: Detect malware behaviour on endpoints and watch for unexpected calls to LLM APIs, since malware may fetch commands or code from a model at run time.
containment_steps: Isolate the affected hosts from the network and preserve memory and disk evidence.
Block the malware's hashes and the LLM API endpoints or keys it uses at the proxy and firewall.
Revoke any API keys or credentials found on the hosts and report abused keys to the AI provider.

AI-assisted command & control.control_family: Network egress control for AI services
AI-assisted command & control.description: Allow only approved AI services and accounts to be reached from internal hosts, and inspect AI-service traffic, because public AI APIs can be used as covert command channels.
containment_steps: Block the AI service accounts, assistants or endpoints used as the relay at the egress proxy.
Isolate hosts that contacted the relay and hunt for the same beaconing pattern across the network.
Report the abused accounts or assistants to the AI provider for takedown.

Prompt injection & jailbreaking.control_family: Input and output guardrails with system-prompt hardening
Prompt injection & jailbreaking.description: Screen prompts and responses with a layered detector and keep the system prompt hardened and versioned, since jailbreak wording changes faster than fixed rules.
containment_steps: Block or rate-limit the session or client that sent the payload and keep the full prompt and response as evidence.
Check whether the response leaked the system prompt or produced restricted content, and record the attack family.
Add the payload and paraphrased variants to the replay set and run the auto-hardening cycle for this attack family.

Poisoning & backdoor.description: Track where training and fine-tuning data come from, validate it before use, and test models for backdoor triggers before release.
containment_steps: Stop serving or roll back the affected model to the last version trained on verified data.
Identify and remove the poisoned samples or data sources, and preserve them for analysis.
Retrain or fine-tune from clean data and re-test for the trigger behaviour before redeploying.

AI supply chain.description: Pin, sign and scan models, datasets, packages and plugins from registries, and keep an AI bill of materials so a malicious artifact can be traced to every system using it.
containment_steps: Remove the malicious artifact from every environment and block its name, version and hash in internal mirrors.
Rotate credentials and secrets that were reachable from systems where the artifact was loaded.
Replace it with a verified version and report the artifact to the registry maintainers.

Extraction, inversion & adversarial.control_family: Model access control and query limits
Extraction, inversion & adversarial.description: Authenticate model access, limit query rates and output detail, and harden models against adversarial inputs.
containment_steps: Suspend the accounts or API keys behind the suspicious query pattern and preserve the query logs.
Lower query limits and reduce output detail such as confidence scores for the affected endpoint.
Assess what model behaviour or training data may have been exposed and notify data owners if needed.

RAG poisoning & data extraction.description: Control who can add content to retrieval sources, check documents before indexing, and enforce the user's access rights at retrieval time.
containment_steps: Remove the poisoned or exposed documents from the index and re-index from trusted sources.
Restrict write access to the knowledge base and review recent contributions.
Identify answers or users affected by the bad retrievals and correct or notify them.

Conversation & hidden-context compromise.description: Keep secrets, credentials and other users' data out of the model's context, and isolate sessions so one conversation cannot read another.
containment_steps: Rotate any secret, key or credential that appeared in the model's context or output.
Purge exposed conversation history and confirm session isolation between users.
Remove the sensitive data from system prompts and tool context, and notify affected users if personal data leaked.

Prompt & memory manipulation.description: Validate and label untrusted content before it enters prompts or saved memory, and let users review and reset what the assistant remembers.
containment_steps: Clear the manipulated memory entries or conversation state for the affected accounts.
Block the source content (page, file or message) that carried the injected instructions.
Review actions or answers given while the manipulation was active and correct them.

Prompt injection against LLM security to.control_family: Layered review of LLM security verdicts
Prompt injection against LLM security to.description: Never let an LLM-based security tool be the only gate: confirm its verdicts with independent detectors or human review, especially for 'safe' verdicts on suspicious input.
containment_steps: Re-scan the evaded files, emails or code with a non-LLM detector and quarantine anything malicious.
Strip or neutralise embedded instructions in inputs before they reach the security tool.
Route high-risk items to human review until the tool is re-tested against this evasion.

Plugin RCE & insecure output handling.description: Treat model output as untrusted: encode it before rendering and run any generated code or plugin call in a sandbox with least privilege.
containment_steps: Disable the vulnerable plugin, renderer or code-execution feature until it is patched.
Check the host or browser sessions where the output executed for compromise and isolate them if needed.
Add output encoding and sandboxing, then re-test with the original payload.

LLM service abuse & cost.description: Protect AI API keys and cloud credentials, and set spending limits, quotas and alerts on LLM usage.
containment_steps: Revoke the stolen or abused API keys and cloud credentials and issue new ones.
Apply spending caps and rate limits on the affected account and stop unauthorised workloads.
Find how the keys leaked (repository, logs, client code) and remove them from there.

Agent tool & API misuse.control_family: Least-privilege agent tools with human approval
Agent tool & API misuse.description: Give agents only the tools and permissions the task needs, treat tool output and retrieved content as untrusted, and require human approval for sensitive actions.
containment_steps: Pause the agent and revoke the tokens and permissions its tools used.
Review the agent's tool-call log to find every action taken and undo or contain each one.
Reduce the agent's tool permissions and require approval for file, network and data-export actions before re-enabling it.

Autonomous offensive operations.description: Expect faster, multi-step attacks run by AI agents: monitor for machine-speed scanning and exploitation, and automate containment of exposed systems.
containment_steps: Block the source infrastructure and isolate the systems that were scanned or exploited.
Patch or take offline the vulnerabilities the agent exploited, starting with internet-facing systems.
Hunt for persistence and data access across the attack chain and report the operator's AI accounts to the provider.

A.control_family: Security awareness and AI-aware threat detection
A.description: Assume attacker tooling is AI-assisted: tune detections and user training for faster, more convincing attacks.
containment_steps: Contain the affected accounts or hosts and preserve evidence.
Block the indicators of compromise linked to the attack.
Review related activity for other victims of the same campaign.

B.description: Protect the model, its training pipeline and its distribution with access control, validation and monitoring.
containment_steps: Restrict access to the affected model or pipeline and preserve logs.
Roll back to the last verified model version if behaviour has changed.
Investigate the attack path and close it before restoring access.

C.description: Secure the application layer around the model: inputs, retrieval, context, output handling and usage.
containment_steps: Disable the affected application feature and preserve request logs.
Rotate any exposed secrets and remove exposed data.
Fix the weakness and re-test with the original input before re-enabling.

D.description: Limit agent autonomy and permissions, log every tool call, and keep a human in the loop for high-impact actions.
containment_steps: Pause the agent and revoke its credentials.
Review its action log and contain each harmful action.
Reduce its permissions and add approval steps before re-enabling.

out_of_scope.description: The Mapper judged this alert out of scope for the attack taxonomy.
containment_steps: No containment needed: the Mapper classified this alert as out of scope.
Spot-check the alert if it was flagged by the detector, to confirm it is not a missed attack.
